fix: Remove/correct the misleading comment or make the default branch explicitly mark the event processed so the 'won't loop forever' guarantee is local.

title: API graceful shutdown does not drain in-flight HTTP requests before closing DB/Redis pools
description: main.ts:41 only app.enableShutdownHooks(). On SIGTERM Nest closes the HTTP server then runs onModuleDestroy; tenant-prisma.service.ts:88-94 does this.cache.clear() then Promise.allSettled(entries.map(e=>e.client.$disconnect())) immediately — it does not wait for active queries to quiesce. redis.service.ts:37-41 quits. No BeforeApplicationShutdown drain delay and no readiness flip; grep confirms no stop_grace_period in compose.
impact: On each redeploy, requests in flight at the SIGTERM instant can have their tenant Prisma client disconnected mid-query, turning in-progress mutations into 500s. Small recurring blast radius (only SIGTERM-window requests).
fix: Add a BeforeApplicationShutdown hook that flips readiness to draining and waits a couple seconds for the LB to stop sending traffic before pools are torn down; set a sensible stop_grace_period.

title: EmailOutbox failure path dead-letters permanently when the post-send re-read returns null/fails
description: On send failure, processOne re-reads the row for the incremented attempts (email-worker.ts:142-146) and computes exhausted = (post?.attempts ?? row.maxAttempts) >= (post?.maxAttempts ?? row.maxAttempts). If the re-read returns null (row deleted) or its query throws transiently, the attempts fallback is row.maxAttempts, which makes exhausted true — so the email is dead-lettered (status 'dead', abandonedAt set, lines 147-151) instead of retried. A transient control-DB read blip right after an SMTP failure thus permanently abandons the email.
impact: A transient control-DB read failure immediately after an SMTP send failure silently drops a reminder/password-reset/announcement email (marked dead, no retry). Narrow window, low frequency, but it's silent data loss of a user-facing notification.
fix: On a null/failed re-read default to the retry branch (treat as not-exhausted) rather than dead-lettering; only dead-letter when attempts are confirmably >= maxAttempts (e.g. re-read with retry or use the increment's returned row).

title: ExportJob.fileBytes and ImportBatch.sizeBytes are Int4 — overflow above ~2 GB
description: schema.prisma:619 `fileBytes Int?` and :1034 `sizeBytes Int @default(0)` are 32-bit (PostgreSQL INTEGER max 2,147,483,647 ≈ 2 GiB), vs :242 `storageUsedBytes BigInt @default(0)`. The export writer sets it from a real on-disk size: export-processors.ts:78 `const bytes = (await fs.stat(outPath)).size;` (and :103 for the zip) → :40 `data: { ... fileBytes: bytes }`. An `all`-scope export bundles control + every tenant DB into one zip (export-processors.ts:62,94-99), so >2 GiB is plausible as catalogues grow. ImportBatch.sizeBytes is set from import.service.ts:72 `sizeBytes: input.file.buffer.byteLength` (limited by upload size, so less likely to overflow, but same type hazard).
impact: Writing the size of a >2 GiB export artifact throws a Postgres out-of-range error on the column write at export-processors.ts:40, failing the bookkeeping update even though the dump itself succeeded. Limited blast radius (large bundled exports as data grows); the import path is bounded by upload limits.
fix: Widen ExportJob.fileBytes and ImportBatch.sizeBytes to BigInt, mirroring Tenant.storageUsedBytes. INTEGER → BIGINT is a safe, non-destructive additive migration.

title: Documented audit-log retention is never enforced — tenant audit_log grows unbounded forever
description: The tenant audit_log model comment (db-tenant/schema.prisma:561-563) states retention is 'governed by the tenant's plan (audit_log_retention_days feature) and enforced by a background job.' No such job exists: the scheduled-job registry (apps/api/src/jobs/registry.ts) registers support-session-expiry, reservation-pickup-expiry, stripe-webhook-retry, fine-accrual, export-file-cleanup, announcement-publish, book-metadata-refresh, member-notifications — nothing prunes audit_log. Grep for auditLogRetention/audit_log_retention/prune/purge across apps/api/src and packages/db-tenant finds only the schema comment and unrelated export-file cleanup. audit_log is the highest-write table (every meaningful mutation writes a row including beforeJson/afterJson blobs).
impact: Each tenant's audit_log grows without bound, eventually dominating per-tenant DB size and degrading the live circulation DB, and the plan's audit_log_retention_days promise is silently unmet (a possible data-retention/compliance gap for libraries that expect old audit data to be purged).
fix: Either implement the retention job (batched DELETE WHERE occurredAt < now() - plan.audit_log_retention_days per tenant, using the existing @@index([occurredAt])) or remove the schema comment's claim that retention is enforced.

title: tenant-relocate verifyDestination passes on an EMPTY restore (only checks table count > 0, not row counts)
description: verifyDestination (tenant-relocate.ts:261-265) only asserts `count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public'` is > 0. Because ensureDestinationDatabase runs `prisma migrate deploy`-equivalent schema setup and pg_restore uses --clean --if-exists, the destination always has the public tables from the schema even if pg_restore restored zero DATA rows (e.g. a silently truncated/partial dump, or pg_restore data errors that don't abort the process). The verify therefore can pass on a destination that has the correct empty schema but no data, after which the control plane is cut over (line 136-139) and the source is later dropped.
impact: A partial/empty restore can be cut over as 'verified', and once --drop-source runs the source is gone — silent data loss for that library. Low likelihood (pg_restore usually errors loudly) but the verification gives false assurance for the irreversible cutover.
fix: Compare a few representative table row counts (or pg_restore's --exit-on-error plus a checksum/row-count diff between source and destination on key tables) before updating tenants.db_url, not just table existence.

title: rclone offsite copy failure aborts but is not alerted; partial/missing offsite copy goes unnoticed
description: With `set -euo pipefail` (line 19), `rclone copy --quiet "$dest" "$RCLONE_REMOTE/$day"` (line 90) aborts the script non-zero on failure, but the only sink is the cron redirect documented at line 14 (`>> /var/log/libriant/backup.log 2>&1`). There is no healthcheck/heartbeat/alert on failure or success. `--quiet` suppresses rclone progress/error detail. The local prune (lines 37-39) runs first and succeeds, so local dailies still roll off at BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (default 14, line 23) while offsite copies stay stale.
impact: Offsite backups can quietly stop (expired token, full Storage Box, network) and the gap is invisible until a restore is attempted; with 14-day local retention, prolonged rclone failure means the only durable copies expire unnoticed.
fix: Emit a success/failure heartbeat to a dead-man's-switch (e.g. healthchecks.io — ping on completion, none on failure) and/or alert on non-zero exit. Drop --quiet or capture rclone stderr into the manifest, and verify offsite object count/size after copy.

title: Password-reset request is a timing-based account-enumeration oracle despite the uniform response
description: request() is NOT uniform-time. password-reset.service.ts:42 returns immediately for missing/inactive tenant (after one findUnique); :48 returns for missing/inactive user (after a second findUnique); only the valid path runs :50 `crypto.randomBytes(32)`, :52-57 a Redis `SET … EX`, body build, and :75 `await this.emails.enqueue(...)`. Contrast login.service.ts:62/67/90/95/98 which deliberately call `this.passwords.dummyVerify` on every miss to equalize timing — password-reset has no such equalization, and auth.controller.ts:135 comments 'Uniform response prevents email-enumeration' which is true only for the response body, not latency.
impact: Latency differences let an attacker distinguish registered (slug,email) pairs from non-existent ones, leaking a tenant's account membership and aiding the credential-stuffing in ratelimit-2. Downgraded from medium to low: the largest delta is the Redis SET + queue enqueue (sub-millisecond to low-ms over a private network), the findUnique queries on the negative paths add their own variable latency that muddies the signal, and exploitation at scale also depends on the missing rate limiting (ratelimit-3). Real but a weak, noisy oracle.
fix: Equalize work on every path (always do a dummy Redis write / fixed delay mirroring login's dummyVerify), and rate-limit the endpoint so any residual timing signal isn't probeable at scale.

title: ISBN-lookup and cover-upload endpoints make/accept unthrottled outbound + heavy requests
description: isbn.controller.ts:14-21 is guarded (TenantGuard+PlanGuard) but has no throttle. On cache miss isbn.service.ts:32 `await fetchOpenLibraryBook(isbn)` → openlibrary.ts:48 `fetch(url)` to openlibrary.org. Redis caches per-isbn; isbn.service.ts:37-38 deliberately does NOT cache transient transport failures (`return null` without writeCache). covers.controller.ts:37-39 accepts a multipart upload up to `storageMaxUploadBytes` with a storage write (:61 `this.storage.put`) and no per-tenant request-rate cap.
impact: An authenticated tenant can drive outbound volume to OpenLibrary (risking Libriant's egress IP being throttled/blocked, degrading the feature for all tenants) and flood per-tenant storage with rapid cover uploads. Lowered from medium to low: requires a valid session AND the isbn_lookup_enabled plan feature, and openlibrary.ts:52 returns null (cached negative for 1h, isbn.service.ts:42) for both 404 and any non-OK HTTP — so distinct valid-shape unknown ISBNs are negatively cached after one hit; only true transport timeouts (openlibrary.ts:46 abort) bypass caching, narrowing the sustained-egress vector to a flaky-upstream scenario.
fix: Add a per-tenant throttle on isbn-lookup and a shared global outbound concurrency/rate cap toward OpenLibrary (reused by the book-metadata-refresh job), plus a per-tenant rate cap on cover uploads.

title: Stripe webhook endpoint is public and unthrottled — signature-verification CPU/log-spam vector
description: stripe-webhook.controller.ts is in the set of controllers with no @UseGuards (confirmed via `grep -L UseGuards` over *.controller.ts), and Caddyfile:156-158 routes `/webhooks/*` straight to api:3001 with no prefix-strip and no rate_limit. Like all other endpoints there is no global throttler (app.module.ts has no APP_GUARD). Security is provided by Stripe signature verification on the raw body (main.ts:13-19 keeps rawBody for this), so forged events are rejected — but each unauthenticated POST still triggers a constructEvent signature computation and an error log before rejection.
impact: Lower severity than the auth endpoints because forged events cannot mutate billing state (signature check stops them). But the public, unthrottled surface lets an attacker burn API CPU on signature verification and flood logs/alerting with rejected-webhook noise. Worth a per-IP throttle once trust-proxy is fixed.
fix: Add a per-IP throttle on /webhooks/* (Caddy rate_limit or @nestjs/throttler) so signature-verification work and error logging can't be driven unbounded by an unauthenticated attacker.

title: notificationTemplates DTO accepts arbitrary unbounded object before service-side sanitization
description: tenant-settings.dto.ts:114-116 `@IsOptional() @IsObject() notificationTemplates?: Record<string, NotificationTemplate>;` — no ValidateNested, no per-field MaxLength, no overall size bound. The service does enforce shape/length: tenant-settings.service.ts:11-13 (TEMPLATE_KINDS = dueSoon/overdue/holdReady, SUBJECT_MAX=200, BODY_MAX=4000) and sanitizeTemplates 16-32 whitelists kinds, keeps only string subject/body, trims and slices to the caps; update() runs it at line 135 and stores only the sanitized result (138). The job-time substitute() only replaces a fixed key set `/\{(member|book|due|by|library)\}/g` (member-notifications.job.ts:103-104) and can't be abused. So oversized/malformed input is accepted by validation, briefly held, JSON-stringified for the no-op diff (tenant-settings.service.ts:137), then discarded — never persisted. Impact is bounded further by the default Express ~100kb JSON body limit. Confirmed low.
impact: Minimal: a malformed or oversized notificationTemplates payload passes DTO validation, is held in memory and JSON.stringify'd for the audit diff, then dropped by sanitizeTemplates. No corruption and no persistence of bad data; the stored value is always whitelisted and length-capped.
fix: Optional hardening: replace @IsObject with a typed nested DTO (a class with optional dueSoon/overdue/holdReady, each ValidateNested to {subject?, body?} carrying @IsString + @MaxLength(200)/@MaxLength(4000)) so oversized/malformed input is rejected at the boundary with a clear 400 and the DTO bounds stay in sync with the sanitizer.

title: Frontmatter parser silently last-wins on duplicate keys and rejects CRLF files; no body size bound
description:
scripts/ingest-help-articles.ts:51-58 loops header lines and does `fm[key] = value` with no duplicate detection. I ran the parser on a file with two slug lines: result `{title:'A', slug:'second', summary:'s'}` — silent last-wins, so the article is upserted/looked-up under an unexpected slug with no warning. Line 42 `if (!raw.startsWith('---
'))` and line 45 `const closeIx = raw.indexOf('
---', 4)` assume LF: I ran the parser on a CRLF file (`---
title: A
...`) and it threw 'missing frontmatter' — any CRLF-saved file is rejected outright. No upper bound on body size before it is stored in the TEXT columns and rendered.
impact: Low / build-time footguns on trusted, checked-in input maintained by the team. A stray duplicate key yields a wrong slug; a CRLF line ending yields a confusing 'missing frontmatter' failure. Both surface at ingest before prod, no runtime or tenant exposure. The unbounded body is harmless for the current trusted source. Robustness/maintainability rather than a live defect — low is correct.
fix: Warn or reject on duplicate frontmatter keys; normalize CRLF (strip \r) before the startsWith check; optionally cap body size. Nice-to-haves given the trusted source, but they remove silent-misparse footguns for future editors.

title: Web ops endpoints (/api/metrics, /api/readyz, /api/healthz) are publicly reachable with no auth
description: Confirmed no middleware exists: `find apps/web -name middleware.ts` returns nothing. Public apex block in Caddyfile (lines 129-164) has only three carve-outs — `handle_path /lbr-api/*` (139), `handle /webhooks/*` (156), and `import static_assets` (=> `handle_path /_assets/*`, line 69) — then a catch-all `handle { reverse_proxy web:3000 }` (161-163). There is NO `/api/*` carve-out, so /api/metrics, /api/readyz, /api/healthz are proxied to Next.js. The `(maintenance_check)` snippet's `@is_probe path /healthz /readyz /metrics` (Caddyfile:59) matches only those bare paths (not /api/...) AND merely returns "ok" 200 — it is an availability helper, not a block. metrics/route.ts:21 emits `libriant_web_build_info{node_env="${process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development'}"} 1` plus uptime (line 18). The three routes contain zero auth references (grep for auth/cookie/session/token returned none). Compose: only caddy publishes ports 80/443 (docker-compose.prod.yml:93-96); web has no `ports:` so it is reachable solely via Caddy's catch-all. The web /metrics route does NOT expose DB URLs/queue depths/tenant counts — disclosure is limited to NODE_ENV + uptime + liveness, as the finding states.
impact: Anonymous external callers (subject only to the general Cloudflare proxy in front, not a route-specific block) can probe web-tier liveness/readiness and learn NODE_ENV. Reconnaissance value only; no secrets. Low blast radius.
fix: Add an ops matcher to both public site blocks that 404s these paths from the internet, e.g. `@ops path /api/metrics /api/readyz /api/healthz` then `handle @ops { respond 404 }` placed before the catch-all `handle`. Expose them only on an internal listener/network for Prometheus and the orchestrator, or gate behind a bearer token / source-IP allowlist.

title: /api/readyz leaks the internal API hostname/connection error to unauthenticated callers
description: readyz/route.ts:31 returns `api: { reachable: false, error: (err as Error).message }` directly in the JSON body on a fetch failure. Target is `process.env.API_INTERNAL_URL ?? process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001'` (lines 13-14). In prod, docker-compose.prod.yml:192 sets `API_INTERNAL_URL: http://api:3001`, so a Node fetch failure surfaces messages like `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api` or `connect ECONNREFUSED <ip>:3001`, disclosing the internal service name and port. Combined with edge-1 (route is publicly reachable, no auth), any anonymous caller hitting it during an API outage receives this. NOTE: the finding's illustrative hostname `api-internal.libriant.internal` overstates it — the actual disclosed value is the conventional Docker service name `api` and port `3001`, which materially lowers the recon value but the raw-error-echo behavior is real.
impact: Internal Docker service name + port (and, on ECONNREFUSED, the container IP) disclosed to unauthenticated callers during an API outage. Low value since `api:3001` is conventional, but it is unintended topology leakage in exactly the window an attacker probes.
fix: Do not echo `(err as Error).message`. Return a generic body, e.g. `{ status: 'not_ready', api: { reachable: false } }`, and `console.error` the detail server-side. Fix together with edge-1 by restricting the endpoint to internal callers.

title: Deploy runs git reset --hard to an unverified SHA with no commit-signature check
description: deploy.yml:155-156 `git fetch --quiet origin` / `git reset --hard ${GIT_SHA}` (GIT_SHA = github.sha, env at line 142). The grep for `verify-commit|verify-tag|gpg|--verify` across .github/ scripts/ infra/ returns nothing. Comment at 144-151 acknowledges host-local tracked-file edits are overwritten (mitigated by keeping customizations in .env.prod, which is outside the tree — accurate).
impact: Defense-in-depth gap only. With an intact SSH session and trusted GitHub the deployed SHA is whatever triggered the workflow, so blast radius is low on its own. It compounds cicd-1: if the SSH transport is MITM'd, there is no provenance check on the code that gets checked out and run. Correctly rated low.
fix: If signed commits/tags are adopted, add `git verify-commit ${GIT_SHA}` (or verify-tag) before `git reset --hard`. Primary fix is cicd-1 (authenticate the transport).

title: Excel import decompresses fully in memory (exceljs/JSZip) — 64 MB upload can expand to GBs (zip-bomb memory DoS)
description: xlsx-parser.ts:42 `await wb.xlsx.load(ab)` loads the entire workbook (exceljs unzips via JSZip into memory) before any row cap; tabular.ts:69 applies `opts.maxRows` only AFTER the full matrix is materialized — so the cap is post-decompression. import.constants.ts:7 `IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024` bounds only the COMPRESSED upload (multer fileSize at import.controller.ts:70). Crucially, parseByFormat runs in BOTH the worker (import-worker.ts:101) and SYNCHRONOUSLY in the API request during createBatch with maxRows: PREVIEW_ROWS (import.service.ts:48-54) — so a crafted xlsx OOMs the API process on upload, not just the worker. exceljs (not SheetJS) is the only spreadsheet dep — verified no `xlsx`/SheetJS package in apps/api/package.json — so SheetJS proto-pollution/ReDoS advisories correctly do not apply.
impact: An authenticated tenant uploading a highly-compressible 64 MB .xlsx can decompress to multiple GB and OOM the importing process. Blast radius is slightly LARGER than the original finding stated: because import.service.ts:48 parses during the upload request, the API process (serving all cell tenants) can be OOM-killed, not only the import worker. Still bounded by single-cell topology and process restart, so low is defensible; the upgraded blast radius is the one correction.
fix: Cap DECOMPRESSED size, not just compressed: inspect zip-entry uncompressed sizes before parsing, or wrap parse in a memory/row budget and abort early; run xlsx parse in a constrained child/worker with a hard memory ceiling; and prefer doing the parse only in the worker rather than synchronously in the upload request.

title: StripeInvoiceShape.subscription is a stale top-level field for the installed dahlia API version (latent, not yet exploited)
description: StripeInvoiceShape declares top-level `subscription: string | null` (stripe-driver.ts:67). In the installed SDK's dahlia Invoice object (esm/resources/Invoices.d.ts:126) there is NO top-level `subscription` field (confirmed: the only `subscription?` hits in the file are inside Create/Update/Preview *param* interfaces at lines 1272/2454/2756, not the object); the linkage lives under `parent: Invoice.Parent | null` → `Parent.subscription_details: Parent.SubscriptionDetails | null` (Invoices.d.ts:651). Today the invoice handlers only read `payload.customer` (billing.service.ts:516,524,525), and `customer` IS still top-level on the Invoice object (Invoices.d.ts: `customer: string | Customer | DeletedCustomer | null`), so nothing breaks now.
impact: No current runtime effect. It is a trap for the billing-4 recommended fix (which wants to scope by subscription) and a sign the hand-written StripeInvoiceShape/StripeSubscriptionShape were written against a pre-basil API and never reconciled with the installed SDK.
fix: When implementing billing-4, read the subscription id from parent.subscription_details.subscription (or expand it explicitly) and update StripeInvoiceShape accordingly. Audit both hand-written shapes against the installed SDK types in one pass — billing-1 is the same class of drift on the Subscription shape.

title: Content-Disposition filename sanitiser does not strip double-quotes (minor header-attribute breakage, not response splitting)
description: sanitiseFilename (storage-demo.controller.ts:217-219) strips only `[\\/\0]` and slices to 200 chars, then the result is interpolated into `content-disposition: attachment; filename="${sanitiseFilename(filename)}"` (line 208). A double-quote (`%22`) in the filename is not removed and would prematurely close the quoted-string in the header. Response splitting via CR/LF is NOT possible because Node's res.set throws on header values containing CR/LF, and the unauthenticated signed route's filename comes from server-signed payload.fn or `ref.split('/').pop()` (line 159) rather than raw user input; the authenticated download route's :filename param would have to also resolve to a real stored file (which uses server-generated cuid names with no quotes) before reaching sendFile, so a crafted quote-bearing filename just 404s at storage.get/stat. Practical impact is therefore negligible — a malformed Content-Disposition attribute at worst.
impact: At most a malformed download filename attribute in an edge case; no header injection / response splitting due to Node's header validation and the cuid-only stored filenames. Informational only.
fix: Also strip or percent-encode double-quotes in sanitiseFilename, or use RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''<encoded>` form.

title: No integration test covers importing a second active loan on the same copy (unique-index path untested)
description: The only loan import test (import-engine.spec.ts:178-186) imports a single active loan and asserts the copy flips to on_loan. There is no test that imports two active loans for the same barcode (or a loan onto an already-on_loan copy), which is exactly the scenario the finder feared. That path relies on the loans_one_active_per_copy partial unique index (migration.sql:458) surfacing as a P2002 row error via dbIssue (import-engine.ts:81-87); without a test, a future refactor (e.g. importing loans outside a transaction, or a schema change dropping the partial index) could silently reintroduce duplicate active loans undetected.
impact: The single most important circulation invariant under import is unverified, so a regression that removes/weakens the DB index or the error mapping would not be caught.
fix: Add an integration test that imports two active-loan rows for the same barcode (and one onto an already-on_loan copy) and asserts the second yields an error row with a duplicate code and that exactly one active loan exists.

title: Export cleanup leaves fileName populated after purging filePath, so listings still advertise a downloadable-looking file
description: The cleanup sweep nulls filePath and fileBytes (`data: { filePath: null, fileBytes: null }`) but leaves fileName set. publicExportJob (export.service.ts:14) returns fileName, so a purged export still shows a fileName in the list UI even though download now 404s. Cosmetic only — the download path correctly rejects on `!job.filePath` (export-download.ts:9). No data exposure.
impact: Minor UX inconsistency: the exports list shows a filename for an export whose file has been purged; clicking download yields a BadRequest. No security or data impact.
fix: Optionally also null fileName in the cleanup update so the listing reflects that the artifact is gone.

title: Help-article HTML rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization (trusted-by-construction today)
description: page.tsx:64 renders `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: article.bodyHtml }}`. The data flow the finder described is accurate: `grep -rn bodyHtml` over apps/packages/scripts shows the field is WRITTEN only by scripts/ingest-help-articles.ts:124 and :133, which renders checked-in markdown via `renderHtml` (ingest-help-articles.ts:92-95: `marked.setOptions({ gfm: true, breaks: false }); return marked.parse(markdown, { async: false })` — no sanitizer/escape configured). The API help.service.ts only READS bodyHtml (lines 123, 140), never writes it, and serves it via GET /help/articles/:slug. So no tenant/end-user input reaches this field today — 'safe by construction' is correct for the current state. The latent risk (marked does not strip raw HTML, so a raw
impact: No exploit today: content is staff-authored, code-reviewed, and committed to the repo. Exposure only materializes if (a) help authoring ever moves to a dynamic/admin-editable surface, or (b) a malicious/compromised markdown file lands in the repo, in which case stored XSS would run in tenant sessions. Correctly rated info.
fix: Sanitize at ingest time — run the marked output through sanitize-html / DOMPurify, or configure marked to escape raw HTML — so the persisted bodyHtml is safe regardless of what a markdown source contains. This decouples safety from the 'checked-in content is trusted' assumption.

title: Per-app lint scripts are stubs ('echo lint: ok') — dead/misleading, though CI's actual lint still covers app code
description: Root package.json `"lint": "eslint ."`; apps/api and apps/web both `"lint": "echo 'lint: ok'"`. ci.yml:48 step `ESLint (all packages)` runs `pnpm lint` which resolves to the ROOT `eslint .` (not `turbo run lint`). eslint.config.mjs:37-38 lints `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` with only build-output ignores (lines 23-33), so `eslint .` does cover apps/api/src and apps/web/. turbo.json defines a `lint` task (lines 13-15) but nothing in CI or root scripts calls `turbo run lint`. The two echo scripts are reachable only via turbo and are effectively dead.
impact: No current coverage gap, but a trap: the stub scripts make per-package linting look configured while doing nothing. A one-line change of the root `lint` to `turbo run lint` (a natural-looking alignment with the other turbo tasks) would silently disable ESLint across the entire app surface while CI stays green.
fix: Replace the two `echo 'lint: ok'` scripts with a real package-scoped `eslint .`, or delete them and document that root `eslint .` is the single source of truth; keep CI on `pnpm lint` (root), not `turbo run lint`.

title: Verified: .env.local is NOT committed and holds no real secrets (prompt premise did not hold)
description: `git ls-files --error-unmatch .env.local` -> 'did not match any file(s)'; `git check-ignore -v .env.local` -> matches `.gitignore:9:.env.local`; `git log --all -- .env.local` -> empty (never committed). `diff .env.local .env.example` -> identical. The only secret-like non-comment line is `.env.local:38 SESSION_SECRET=dev-only-session-secret-CHANGE-IN-PROD` (dev placeholder). No live credentials. Also confirmed `git ls-files | grep .env` lists only .env.example and .env.prod.example (both templates).
impact: None — closes the loop on the prompt's premise. Env-file secret hygiene is correct: dev placeholders only, file properly ignored.
fix: No action required. Optionally add a gitleaks/trufflehog secret-scanning step to ci.yml (there is currently none) to catch future accidental secret commits.

title: Help search query and slug lookup are properly parameterized — no SQL injection (lane goal verification)
description: apps/api/src/help/help.service.ts:79-95: `controlDb.$queryRawUnsafe(`...`, config, q, locale, limit)` — the SQL is a constant template; the user query reaches Postgres only as bind param $2 in `plainto_tsquery($1::regconfig, public.immutable_unaccent($2))` (lines 84, 87). No user input is string-concatenated into the SQL. config ($1) is server-derived `locale === 'en' ? 'english' : 'simple'` (line 78), never user-controlled. limit is clamped `Math.max(1, Math.min(50, input.limit ?? 20))` (line 54) and parseLimit (apps/api/src/platform/query.ts:13-16) collapses non-numeric/≤0 input to undefined. The single-article path uses Prisma findFirst({ where: { slug, locale, archivedAt: null } }) (lines 114-115) with English fallback (lines 130-143), fully ORM-parameterized. No LIKE/ILIKE concatenation anywhere in the module. Verified the verdict is accurate (note: the finding says config is $1 — correct).
impact: None — recorded to close out the SQL-injection question in the lane brief. Search and fetch paths are safe against injection.
fix: No action needed.

title: Asset route serves any file type under ASSETS_ROOT and does not resolve symlinks
description: resolveAssetPath (assets-server.ts:42-49) runs `path.normalize(...).replace(/^[/\\]+/,'')` then `path.resolve(ASSETS_ROOT, ...)` and rejects unless `full.startsWith(ASSETS_ROOT + path.sep) || full === ASSETS_ROOT`. I reproduced the logic in node: `../package.json`, `..`, `../assets-sibling/x`, `../../etc/passwd`, `./../../etc/passwd` all => null; `brand/logo.svg`, `manifest.json`, `README.md` resolve inside. Traversal protection is sound. Residual gaps both confirmed: (1) route.ts:26 falls back to `application/octet-stream` for unknown extensions, so any file under ASSETS_ROOT is served — manifest.json, theme/tokens.json, README.md are all fetchable (verified they exist under /assets); today none hold secrets (client-visible by design). (2) resolveAssetPath does not call fs.realpath, so a symlink planted inside ASSETS_ROOT would be followed by fs.readFile (route.ts:24). `find /assets -type l` returned no symlinks today, and planting one requires filesystem write access — theoretical.
impact: Defense-in-depth gap only; no current exposure. An operator accidentally placing a non-public file under /assets, or a compromise able to write a symlink into the assets bind-mount, would yield arbitrary-file read via the public /_assets route.
fix: Return 404 for any extension not in the MIME table rather than defaulting to octet-stream, and add an `fs.realpath` check after resolveAssetPath asserting the real path still lies under ASSETS_ROOT before fs.readFile.

title: Dependency versions verified — not typosquats, no applicable known advisories on the flagged packages
description: apps/api/package.json declares archiver ^7.0.1 (:23), exceljs ^4.4.0 (:29), fast-xml-parser ^5.8.0 (:30), multer ^2.1.1 (:34), nodemailer ^8.0.9 (:36). pnpm-lock.yaml resolves each with a real sha512 integrity hash (e.g. exceljs@4.4.0 sha512-XctvKaEM..., multer@2.1.1 sha512-mo+QTzKl..., nodemailer@8.0.9 sha512-5ofa7BUN..., fast-xml-parser@5.8.0 sha512-6bIM7fsJ..., archiver@7.0.1 sha512-ZcbTaIqJ...; transitive archiver@5.3.2 also present) — not fabricated/typosquatted. marc-parser.ts:142-149 builds XMLParser with ignoreAttributes:false/removeNSPrefix/parseTagValue:false and NO DOCTYPE/external-entity option (fast-xml-parser does not expand external entities/DTD by default) — XXE/billion-laughs not a vector. All five FileInterceptor sites set limits.fileSize (branding.controller.ts:55, covers.controller.ts:39, storage-demo.controller.ts:58, photos.controller.ts:39, import.controller.ts:70). Confirmed ci.yml has NO pnpm audit / Dependabot step (jobs are static-checks, unit-tests, integration-tests, db-migration only).
impact: No action required for these specific packages; the dependency-CVE/typosquat hunt was performed and came back clean. The one actionable sub-point is accurate: ci.yml has no dependency-audit gate to catch FUTURE advisories.
fix: Keep pinned via lockfile; add a `pnpm audit --prod` (or Dependabot/Renovate) step to ci.yml so newly-disclosed advisories on these and other deps are surfaced.
